name: Straw Man
shortDef: Distorting someone's view so it's easier to knock down.
definition: Replacing someone's actual position with an exaggerated, oversimplified or extreme version, then attacking that version as if it were what they said.
howToSpot: Compare what was actually said with the version being attacked.
Look for dropped qualifiers like "some", "sometimes" or "for now".
Would the original speaker accept this summary of their view?
classicExample: She wants fewer cars downtown, so apparently she wants to ban driving and make everyone walk to work.
legitimateVersion: Spelling out the realistic consequences of someone's actual proposal is fair, as long as you describe it accurately and they would recognize your summary.

contrast.fal_red_herring: A straw man distorts the other side's position; a red herring changes the subject to something else entirely.
contrast.fal_false_dichotomy: A straw man misrepresents one view; a false dichotomy pretends only two options exist.
